findings.evidence: docs/cache-infrastructure.md covers only the R2/Lake artifact cache; grep for `mathlib-ltar` matches only .github/workflows/ci.yml and pr-build.yml.
findings.fix: Add a short "Mathlib download cache (GitHub Actions)" section: what is cached (`$MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR/*.ltar`), who publishes (ci.yml on main only), the key/restore-key shape, that entries are immutable, and the recovery steps (bump `mathlib-ltar-v1` in both workflows, or `gh cache delete`).
findings.issue: The repo's cache doc ("Where the build cache lives, who owns it, and which knob feeds which workflow") is not updated for the new GitHub-Actions `.ltar` layer. Operator-facing state introduced here — the `mathlib-ltar-v1` key namespace, main-only publisher / restore-only consumers, pruning to the pin, and the recovery procedure for a poisoned immutable entry — exists only as a YAML comment.

findings.evidence: ci.yml:104-114 — the `if !` branch fires on any nonzero exit; `mathlib/Cache/Requests.lean:794` (`IO.FS.createDirAll IO.CACHEDIR`) means `[ -e "$MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR" ]` is true even with nothing restored.
findings.fix: Reword to what is actually known, e.g. "::warning::lake exe cache get failed; discarding any local .ltar store and forcing a full refetch", and rename the step to "Fetch Mathlib oleans, retrying from an empty download cache" (ci.yml:104).
findings.issue: The warning text and the step name assert a cause the code never established: `lake exe cache get` fails far more often for network/server reasons, and on a total restore miss there is no "restored snapshot" at all (the directory exists only because the cache tool created it). A maintainer reading the log will misdiagnose a Mathlib server outage as a poisoned cache. Same text at pr-build.yml:398.

findings.evidence: pr-build.yml:377-379 — both the exact key and the restore-key prefix embed `hashFiles('base/lean-toolchain')`.
findings.fix: Qualify it: the incremental fallback exists only for a Mathlib-only bump; a `lean-toolchain` bump misses both keys and refetches from the Mathlib server.
findings.issue: "For a validated pin bump ... an exact new-pin snapshot is preferred and the newest same-toolchain main snapshot is the incremental fallback" is wrong for a toolchain bump: `hashFiles('base/lean-toolchain')` is inside the restore-key prefix too, so a toolchain bump has no fallback and restores nothing. ci.yml:76 states the same idea correctly ("the same-toolchain prefix").

findings.evidence: ci.yml:85,87 and pr-build.yml:377,379 both carry the literal `mathlib-ltar-v1`.
findings.fix: Match pr-build.yml: "Bump `mathlib-ltar-v1` in both workflows (see pr-build.yml) ...".
findings.issue: "Bump `mathlib-ltar-v1` if an incompatible or poisoned immutable entry must be abandoned" omits that the same literal is hardcoded in pr-build.yml; bumping only here silently kills all PR-side restores. pr-build.yml:369 says "in both workflows" — the instruction is one-sided only in ci.yml.

findings.evidence: ci.yml:68-78 — one continuous comment block ending at the `Restore Mathlib's compressed download cache` step; the `Build` step is at ci.yml:116 with no comment.
findings.fix: Split it back out as its own comment block immediately above the `- name: Build` step (or above the audits), leaving the restore comment self-contained.
findings.issue: The pre-existing "No aggregator check: the root TauCeti.lean is intentionally empty..." note is now joined by a bare `#` to the new cache-restore rationale, so it reads as documentation of the restore step it precedes; the Build step it explained moved to line 116.

summary: The inline rationale is mostly accurate, but three comments/messages state more than the code establishes (the failure-cause warning, the pin-bump fallback claim, the one-sided key-bump instruction), and the repo's cache-infrastructure doc is left with no mention of the new cache layer or its escape hatch.
